note.1: “The end of the home gas era” describes where the brand sees home heating and cooling heading: electric heat pumps with phase-change storage could replace the gas appliances in a home. It does not mean gas heating or gas water heaters are obsolete or being withdrawn; when choosing, consider your local gas supply, your home and your own preferences.
note.2: The “24 kW” of instant hot water is the dynamic heat output measured in the lab under specific conditions; in use, the output adjusts to the conditions and the load.
note.3: The “10×” energy efficiency vs. gas is the ratio between this product's dynamic heating efficiency (COP ≈ 6) and a gas boiler's (COP ≈ 0.6). A COP of 6 is the highest value measured in the lab under specific conditions; real efficiency varies with the setting, water temperatures and load.
note.4: “50 L in size, the heat of 200 L” means that 50 L of iPCM salt-hydrate phase-change material, tuned at the molecular level, stores 5 kWh under standard conditions. In summer, with water coming in at 20 °C and out at 40 °C, that equals in theory the usable heat of a 215 L tank. It does not mean the PCM500 unit is 50 L in volume, nor that it can replace the whole output of any 200 L tank.
note.5: “5× the heat density of water”: under standard conditions the iPCM material stores over 440 MJ/m³, about 5.2 times as much as water and 2.7 times as much as paraffin; measured in the lab under specific conditions.
note.6: “Each room within ±1 °C” refers to how precisely the floor heating's water temperature is held (±1 °C); in use, the set temperature, the flow and the number of outlets in use at once can cause deviations.
note.7: “Warm floors in 16 minutes”: the PCM500 warms 80 m² of floor heating by 2 °C in 16 minutes, the PCM400 60 m². Measured when starting the floor heating in a reference home; the real speed depends on the starting room temperature, the floor area, how densely the pipes are laid, the building's insulation and more.
note.8: “Fresh air for every room”: the system supports a separate fresh-air module in each room; the modules are sold separately.
note.9: “Free hot water in summer” counts as zero energy when summer cooling recovers enough heat, leaving out the recovery pump: it draws 100 W, so 24 hours of running use 2.4 kWh. If your air conditioning does not recover enough heat, the unit heats water as a heat-pump water heater, which is not recovered heat. The hot water cost leaves out the zero-cold-water mode: with it on, the water left cooling in the pipes is heated again, which costs extra.
note.10: “Half-price floor heating in winter”: calculated for 120 m² of floor heating over a 3-month winter, against a grade 2 efficiency boiler under the Chinese standard GB 20665-2015. Real costs vary with insulation, habits, the local climate and electricity prices.
note.11: “26% cheaper than an air-source heat pump” and “57% cheaper than a gas boiler” are energy cost estimates from a simulation: a region with hot summers and cold winters, 200 m² of floor heating, a 3-month heating season a year, 200 L of hot water a day, electricity at ¥0.62/kWh and gas at ¥3/m³. The floor heating is off 10 hours a day (8:00–18:00); heat loss is taken as 60 W/m², so 60 × 180 × 10 = 108,000 Wh = 108 kWh a day. Heating costs about ¥8,890 with a grade 2 gas boiler, ¥5,190 with a standard air-source heat pump and about ¥3,780 with Jidacheng. Real savings vary with the home, the climate, the energy mix and energy prices.
note.12: “Overturned” is marketing language: with phase-change storage and full heat recovery, this product gets past the engineering limit of conventional air-source heat pumps, which heat only on demand and cannot store heat. It does not mean the product beats every conventional heat pump in every respect.

m.plans.note1: The home sizes above are only a quick guide: the right system depends on the layout, the ceiling height, the building materials and more, and must be sized to the home's real cooling load. For your own system design, contact your local store.
m.plans.note2: The package prices include standard installation, as defined by ORVIBO's installation policy for V-series integrated HVAC packages.
m.plans.note3: The package prices do not include laying the floor heating, which is charged separately by the area laid.
m.plans.note4: The package prices do not include the fresh-air modules: ¥1,999 per room.
m.plans.note5: Special installations: the package prices do not include materials and labour for unusual layouts, longer copper piping, electrical upgrades, drilling through walls and the like; these are quoted after a site survey.
m.plans.note6: Warranty: the warranty period and scope for installation and materials are those of the sales contract and the installation service terms, and may differ from the main unit's warranty.
